notes: This matrix is intentionally advisory. Run `node qa/core/cli.mjs eval-tools --online` to verify docs are reachable, then do the required local spikes before adopting any external tool.

tools.name: Autonoma
tools.license: Vendor describes it as open source / BSL 1.1; verify repository license before adoption.
tools.fit: Closest match to the requested product shape: AI-generated end-to-end tests, self-healing execution, browser/mobile scope, and codebase-informed planning.
tools.recommendation: Evaluate before rebuilding similar functionality. Do not adopt until self-hosting, local-model routing, artifact export, and license posture are proven.
risks: May assume hosted platform workflows or GitHub App integration.
May still require hosted AI configuration unless self-hosted local model support is validated.
BSL is source-available, not OSI open source; legal/usage fit must be confirmed.
required_spike: Self-host locally against CORSIA with no paid service and no cloud API key.
Point it at a local OpenAI-compatible model and run a small auth/settings flow.
Confirm it can export durable local reports and artifacts that future coding agents can read.

tools.name: Vercel agent-browser
tools.fit: Good agent-facing browser control layer for snapshots, screenshots, console/error inspection, traces, and screenshot diffs.
tools.recommendation: Use as an exploration/debug adapter around deterministic Playwright tests, not as the sole regression engine.
risks: Does not by itself generate and maintain a comprehensive test suite.
Natural-language browser control still depends heavily on model discipline.
required_spike: Open a local CORSIA E2E server and capture accessibility snapshots plus annotated screenshots.
Check whether screenshot diff output can feed `qa review` cleanly.
Measure latency with Qwen 35B-class local model in a 5-step flow.

tools.name: Browser Use
tools.fit: Useful autonomous browser-task framework with OpenAI-compatible and local provider options.
tools.recommendation: Evaluate for exploratory QA and coverage discovery, but keep deterministic regression testing in Playwright.
risks: Docs warn that many Qwen models can emit incorrect action schemas without concrete examples.
Repeated regression tests should not depend on an LLM choosing every click.
required_spike: Run a local Qwen-compatible endpoint through Browser Use with strict action-schema examples.
Verify failures produce useful artifacts and not just chat transcripts.
Compare flake rate against direct Playwright tests for the same CORSIA flow.

tools.name: Playwright
tools.fit: Best deterministic execution layer for browser automation, traces, screenshots, visual comparisons, and accessibility snapshots.
tools.recommendation: Use as the stable pass/fail substrate regardless of which AI layer is adopted.
risks: Visual baselines vary across OS/browser/rendering environments unless pinned.
Does not generate or maintain tests by itself.
required_spike: Keep CORSIA smoke tests green in isolated workspace.
Add visual and ARIA baselines for the design-system route and app shell.
